note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing for several weeks with associated chest pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports difficulty swallowing over the past several weeks. Pain occurs when swallowing, located in the chest area. Symptoms are worse with larger pieces of food and do not occur every time patient eats. Patient notes stress over the past couple of months related to moving from west coast to east coast, which has affected diet with increased consumption of pizza and burgers. Patient has also noticed some epigastric pain. Denies weight loss; reports weight gain instead.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Denies blood in stool or dark tarry stool. Reports occasional epigastric pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is relocating from west coast to east coast, which is causing significant stress. Planning to drive for the move due to concerns about traveling with pet dog. Increased alcohol and caffeine consumption noted over past couple of months during stressful period.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 133/70, heart rate normal, no fever, oxygen saturation 100%, respiratory rate 19. Recent weight gain of 10 pounds over last month noted.
Head/Neck: No oral ulcers, no thrush, tonsils midline, no cervical adenopathy, no thyromegaly.
Abdomen: Nondistended with active bowel sounds. Pain to palpation of epigastric area. Negative Murphy's sign, no peritoneal signs, no rebound tenderness.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Skin: No rash, lesions, or bruising.
Eyes: Equal and reactive to light.

RESULTS
Barium swallow study revealed two areas of mild narrowing in the mid and lower portions of the esophagus consistent with esophagitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute esophagitis. Started Protonix 40 mg once daily in the morning. Started Carafate 1 gram four times daily for one month to coat the lining of esophagus and stomach. Upper endoscopy scheduled for next week. Instructed to decrease alcohol and caffeine intake, eat slowly, chew food more thoroughly, and avoid citrus fruits and spicy foods until symptoms improve. Encouraged to focus on healthy eating and dietary changes once settled after move. Follow-up appointment next week for endoscopy procedure.
